Where in the app:

What it says:

What it should say:

Hi everyone.

I'm excited to be here today to talk about CueCard's *teleprompter*.

[smile and pause]

It scrolls your script at _your_ pace, so your eyes stay up and your words stay on track.

[pause]

[anchor]

Leave the app and it keeps going in a floating window, right over your camera or your video call.

[slow down]

Lost your place? Drag the script back. Running long? Skip ahead to the next anchor.

And the timer turns yellow near the end… and red if you get a _little_ too passionate.

[light chuckle]

[anchor]

And these colored words?

[emphasize]

Those are your cues. Reminders to smile, pause, or *not panic*. They're never meant to be read out.

[pause]

[anchor]

Try it out. I think you'll *love* it.

Hi everyone. Introducing *Cue Cards*. [smile]
[separator]
One thought per card. Swipe to the next one when _you're_ ready.
[separator]
The timer at the top keeps you *honest*. [light chuckle]
[separator]
Colored words are cues, not lines. [emphasize]
[separator]
Thanks for listening. *Questions?*
This intentionally crashes the app to verify Crashlytics reporting.
Countdown is the time before the script starts scrolling.
The editor has changes that aren\'t saved. Restoring replaces them with this version.
Swipe right to bring the last card back, or start over.
No account needed. Scripts stay on this device.
In your library, choose Teleprompter or Cards from the menu at the top left, then tap + at the bottom. Teleprompter scrolls your whole script. Cards shows it one card at a time.
Cues are reminders like [pause], shown in color and not read out. Type [ or tap Add Cue above the keyboard.
Tap the timer at the bottom of the editor to set how long you have, when it warns you, and the colors it turns.

When there are changes to save, the bottom of the editor says Unsaved and Save appears at the top. Tap it to save. To keep your changes as a separate script, open ⋮ at the top of the editor, then Save as New. A new script you haven\'t saved shows in the library as a draft.
In your library, tap ⋮ › Import File to add a text file or a TextPack as a script.
Go Back to an Older Version
Every save is a new version. Tap the version number at the bottom of the editor to compare changes and restore one. Once a note has more than one, it\'s also under ⋮ at the top, in Version History.
In your library, touch and hold a script and tap Share. It\'s sent as text, cues included. A script with images is sent as a TextPack, with its images.
Tap the gear in your library or the editor. Text sizes and cue color are under Teleprompter and Cards, and each keeps its own.
The buttons fade while the script scrolls so they stay out of the way. Tap the screen to show them again.
Drag the script to go back or skip ahead. It keeps scrolling from where you leave it.
Scroll Speed in Settings sets how many lines pass each minute.
Leave CueCard while the teleprompter is open and your script keeps going in a floating window, handy on video calls. It doesn\'t open while the camera is on.
Know When Time Is Running Out
The timer changes color when you\'re near the end and again once you\'re over time. Pick the colors in the timer.
Each box in the editor is one card. Tap Create New Card to add another.
Swipe, or tap Back and Next. The dots at the top show which card you\'re on.
The time at the top counts down your timer. With no timer set, it counts up from when you started.
Select words and tap B or I above the keyboard. Or type *bold* or _italic_.
That file is larger than 10 MB, so it can\'t be imported.

This script is too long to share.
Enter a title for your note

Add your script here...

Tap Add Cue to drop in a delivery reminder, or type [ to write one yourself.

For example: Welcome everyone [smile and pause]
One thought per card.\n\nType [ or tap Add Cue for reminders like [pause].

What happened:

What you expected:

Steps to reproduce:
What would you like CueCard to do?\n
Modes, cues, formatting, images and cards
Collections, saving, import, versions and sharing
Text size, colors, camera, timer and language
Scrolling, recording, mirroring and the floating window
Turning cards, recording and the timer
In the teleprompter\'s timer, set a Countdown to get a few seconds before the script starts scrolling.
Tap the gear, then Language. CueCard is in English, French, Portuguese, Russian and Spanish.
Record a video while the teleprompter is open, even with it floating over the camera, and it shows up here.
CueCard can find the videos you record while the teleprompter is open, and keep each one with its script. They stay in your gallery.
CueCard can\'t see your videos, so it can\'t find the ones you recorded with this script. Allow access in Settings.
CueCard can only see the videos you\'ve chosen, so some takes may be missing.
Tap a take to play it and add tags and notes. Your videos stay in your gallery, and nothing leaves this device.
What worked, and what to change next time
The videos you record with a script

Videos you record in CueCard with a script or deck open are kept as its takes, and so are videos you record in another app while the teleprompter floats over it. Tap the film button next to Play to see them, or the takes beside a script in your library.
Tap a take to play it right in CueCard. Below the video, add tags and notes, like what worked and what to change next time.
Tap the heart on a take. It\'s a favorite in your gallery too.
Swipe left on a take, or play it and tap Delete. It\'s deleted from your gallery too.
Your videos stay in your gallery, and nothing leaves this device.
Allow camera and microphone access in Settings to record videos.
Camera is not ready. Try again.
The camera stopped. Close and reopen the camera to try again.
Camera or microphone unavailable. Try again on a device with a camera.

Tap the camera at the top, tapping the screen first if the buttons are hidden. The camera opens in a small window over your script. Tap the red button to record and again to pause, then tap stop to save the video to your gallery. Your script stays out of the video.
Record in Step with the Script

With the camera open, Play starts recording and Pause pauses it. Recording or pausing on the camera plays or pauses the script, and stopping pauses it. Turn off Sync with Teleprompter in Settings to use them separately.

Tap the camera at the top. The camera opens in a small window over your cards. Tap the red button to record and again to pause, then tap stop to save the video to your gallery. Keep turning cards while you record.
Drag the camera window to any corner. Pinch or double-tap it to change its size, and tap it to hide or show its buttons. Use the buttons to zoom or flip the camera.
An image couldn\'t be added. Try again.
Anchors mark spots in your script, like [anchor]. Type one or tap Add Anchor above the keyboard. In the teleprompter, the buttons at the far left and right jump to the anchor before or after.
Tap the photo above the keyboard to add images from your gallery, or paste one in. Copy an image to paste it into another app.
That file is larger than 100 MB, so it can\'t be imported.
This script couldn\'t be shared. Try again.
Turn on Flip Horizontally or Flip Vertically under Teleprompter in Settings to flip the text for a teleprompter\'s glass. The floating window uses the same settings. Both are off by default.
The pointer at the side of the script marks the line to read. Drag it up or down to read where it suits your eyes, and the script lines up with it. Turn off Reading Guide Line in Settings to hide it.
The deck as you write it.
Each card as you read it.

Your scripts are only kept in CueCard until it\'s back. Choose it again if it moved.
Plays and pauses with the camera.
Tap + below to start a deck of cards.
Tap + below to write a script for the teleprompter.
Keeps your words in view over the camera.
Light, dark, or match your phone.
The new deck you started isn\'t saved. Opening another in its place loses it.
The new script you started isn\'t saved. Opening another in its place loses it.
“%1$s” has changes that aren\'t saved. Opening another script in its place loses them.
CueCard opens on your library, with every script and deck you saved. Tap one to write in it, and tap back to return. Switch between Teleprompter and Cards at the top.
In your library, touch and hold a script, or swipe it. In the editor, tap the title at the bottom to rename it.

In your library, tap + after your collections, or ⋮ › New Collection. Tap a collection at the top to show only its scripts, or All to show every one. To add a script to one, swipe it right or touch and hold it, then tap Add to Collection. A script you start or import goes in the collection you\'re in. Touch and hold a collection to rename or delete it. Tap ⋮ › Sort By to change the order.
Keep Scripts if the App Is Removed

Until you choose a storage folder, scripts are kept only in CueCard and are deleted with the app. In your library, tap ⋮ › Choose Storage Folder. Each script is kept there as a text file, with a list of the collections they\'re in.
There\'s no account, and CueCard doesn\'t upload your scripts. They\'re kept on this device, and in the storage folder if you choose one.

In Settings, under Camera, pick the resolution, frame rate, dynamic range and stabilization. Each camera records as close to them as it can. Turn on Mirror Front Camera to record the front camera as you see it.

Your script or cards are drawn over the camera window, so you can read every line. Turn off Text Above Camera in Settings, under Camera, to show the camera on top instead. Either way, the text stays out of the video.
